insider_note: Walli's formula turns what would otherwise be a repeated reduction-formula derivation into a single substitution — always quote it directly for ∫₀^(π/2) sinⁿx or cosⁿx dx.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State Walli's formula for even n
steps.margin_note: First mark. n=4 is even, so the π/2 factor is included.
steps.memory_tip: Even n ⇒ the formula ends in π/2; odd n ⇒ the formula ends in 1.
lines: When n is even, ∫₀^(π/2) sinⁿx dx
steps.why: Walli's reduction formula gives a closed form for ∫₀^(π/2) sinⁿx dx directly, avoiding a repeated integration-by-parts derivation; an extra factor π/2 appears whenever n is even.
common_mistakes: Using the odd-n version of the formula (which has no trailing π/2) for this even n=4 case.
Missing a factor in the descending product.

steps.label: Substitute n=4 and evaluate
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 3/8 × π/2 = 3π/16 — a direct multiplication once the ratio is found.
steps.memory_tip: (n−1)(n−3)··· down to 1 or 2 sits on top; n(n−2)··· down to 1 or 2 sits on the bottom.
steps.why: Substituting n=4 into the descending products (3·1) over (4·2) gives 3/8, and multiplying by the extra π/2 factor gives the final value.
common_mistakes: Multiplying 3/8 by π instead of π/2.
Reversing numerator and denominator of the product ratio.
